knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly states what least squares minimises and what the slope estimate means for Y versus X?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the OLS criterion and slope interpretation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: OLS minimises sum of squared residuals. Slope is change in mean Y per unit X. Correlation and LAD are different objects.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Minimises sum of squared residuals. Slope: change in mean Y per unit X.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating OLS with software Fit or confusing slope with correlation.

choices.label: Least squares minimises the sum of squared residuals. The slope estimate is the change in mean Y per unit change in X in the simple linear model frame.
Least squares minimises the sum of absolute residuals; the slope equals the sample correlation Corr(X, Y) by definition.
Least squares means clicking Fit in software; no closed-form criterion need be stated once β̂ is printed.
The slope estimate is the ratio of standard deviations SD(Y)/SD(X) with no intercept adjustment; least squares minimises R-squared.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Simple linear model Y = β₀ + β₁ x + ε with data pairs (xi, yi). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: State the criterion and slope; refuse Fit-as-criterion.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The criterion is sum of squared residuals. The slope formula uses covariance over variance. Correlation lacks the SD scaling of the OLS slope.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Minimise sum squared residuals; β̂₁ = Cov̂/Var̂; refuse Fit-as-criterion and Corr-as-slope.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting Fit as the criterion or Corr(X, Y) as the OLS slope.

choices.label: Choose β₀, β₁ to minimise sum (yi minus β₀ minus β₁ xi) squared. Slope β̂₁ = sum (xi minus x-bar)(yi minus ȳ) / sum (xi minus x̄) squared = Cov̂(X, Y) / Var̂(X); intercept β̂₀ = ȳ minus β̂₁ x̄. Fit implements OLS but is not the criterion; Corr(X, Y) is not the OLS slope.
Least squares is clicking Fit; the closed-form slope formula is optional once software returns β̂.
The OLS slope equals Corr(X, Y) because both measure linear association on the same scale.
Minimise sum |yi minus β₀ minus β₁ xi|; the resulting slope is Cov̂(X, Y) / Var̂(X) for simple linear regression.

worked_example.title: OLS slope and intercept for four marine cargo points
worked_example.problem_statement: Four (voyage risk band, cargo loss) pairs (x, y) with y in £000 are (2, 4), (3, 6), (4, 7), (5, 9). Fit the simple linear model y = β₀ + β₁x by ordinary least squares: compute x̄, ȳ, S_xx, S_xy, then β̂₁ and β̂₀. Also report the residual at x = 4.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compute x̄ and ȳ first, then S_xx and S_xy, before forming β̂₁ = S_xy/S_xx.

steps.label: Sample means
steps.attempt_cue: Average the four x values and the four y values.
steps.explanation: OLS formulas centre on the sample means of X and Y.

steps.label: Corrected sums of squares and products
steps.attempt_cue: Compute S_xx = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² and S_xy = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)(yᵢ − ȳ).
steps.explanation: S_xx measures spread in X; S_xy measures co-movement of X and Y about their means.

steps.label: Slope, intercept, and residual at x = 4
steps.attempt_cue: β̂₁ = S_xy/S_xx, β̂₀ = ȳ − β̂₁ x̄, residual = y − (β̂₀ + β̂₁x).
steps.explanation: Least squares minimises Σ residual²; the closed forms give the unique minimisers for simple linear regression.

worked_example.final_answer: β̂₁ = 1.6, β̂₀ = 0.9; fitted line ŷ = 0.9 + 1.6x; residual at x = 4 equals −0.3 (£000).
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using S_xy/S_yy for the slope, or reporting the residual as ŷ − y instead of the convention e = y − ŷ.
